findings.reason: The protected source is already concise, conventional, and expert-interview quality. `slots` and `items` name the two blocking predicates, `lock` identifies the deque's critical section, and each public method exposes its synchronization order directly. There is no needless abstraction, duplicated state, obscure trick, or prohibited exact `index` binding, so an inert candidate would not materially improve it.

An enqueue reserves one of exactly `capacity` slot permits before mutating the deque, so stored elements cannot exceed the bound. A dequeue reserves a published item permit before removal, so it cannot pop an empty deque. Each method mutates under the shared mutex and publishes the opposite permit afterward. `appendleft` plus `pop` returns elements in enqueue linearization order, while waiting before acquiring the mutex lets an opposite operation establish progress. `size` reads the same protected deque state.

An independently implemented condition-variable queue agreed with the protected and immutable native sources on all eight authored fixtures and on 120 deterministic randomized legal schedules generated with seed 1188, for 384 total authored and randomized implementation runs. Random schedules used balanced enqueue/dequeue multisets, capacities 1 through 30, both producer-first and consumer-first arrival orders, optional staggering, payload endpoints, and up to 39 queue-method calls including final size.

The concurrency harness now observes explicit blocking checkpoints after prerequisite operations complete. Source example 1 checks both its empty dequeue and its full-queue enqueue; dedicated capacity-one, consumer-first, and full-producer trials reinforce those predicates. A deliberately unbounded lock-and-deque control still produced the same final values but is now rejected specifically because its second enqueue completes while a capacity-one queue is full. A permanently blocked control is terminated by the isolated timeout.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode concurrency problem 1188, Python, and source-native class entrypoint `BoundedBlockingQueue`. Fresh authenticated evidence confirms the front-in/rear-out API, blocking on full and empty states, producer-only and consumer-only worker roles, final `size()` call, scheduler-dependent concurrent order, payload and workload bounds, and the interview prohibition on a built-in bounded blocking queue.

The app-local and immutable native sources remain byte-identical at SHA-256 65c21b1bea5b24a6e3c941fb9cf65615c9acf8d9c153f58c20a3abc6396fb61f, and the native artifact remains bound to verified submission 2067908712. Constructor state, semaphore acquisition and publication, mutex boundaries, deque orientation, return values, and `size` behavior therefore have no adapter divergence.

The unchanged Original-18 `bounded_concurrency` certificate is the correct route: legal tests have capacity at most 30 and at most 40 queue-method calls, so scheduler-dominated scaling would not be an honest complexity verdict. Protected and native real-tests each passed 8/8 correctness cases with zero benchmark tiers, `runtime_check` false, exact method `bounded_concurrency`, and a passing certificate. The prescribed recovery gate passed 403 tests and 205 subtests, covering certificates, special environments, validators, scheduler semantics, and deadlock handling.

The Approach accurately derives the two counting semaphores, the deque mutex, post-mutation permit publication, append-left/pop-right FIFO orientation, and the rule never to wait while holding the mutex. Its O(1) completed-call work explicitly excludes scheduler-dependent waiting, and O(c) space accounts for the at-most-capacity deque plus constant synchronization state.

The modular Reference preserves the complete class interface and concurrency model, both exact source inputs and outputs, every explanatory event in example 1, all six scheduler-permitted dequeue orders in example 2, all six source constraints, and the source-native built-in-queue note. It adds no source-absent example, hint, follow-up, table, image, or diagram.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed two explained examples, six constraints, one separate note, no hints or follow-up, and no images, tables, or diagrams. `source_fidelity.json` binds every composed section to live statement hash e10a5defa7f88f38ba50d91f3fbdff468f0bcbc88318c9c3a3e0a573fcb9c3b1 and validates without errors.

coverage: The first two visible sample cases are the two authenticated source examples in source order. They preserve the exact constructor and operation arguments plus the exact source outputs; their structured expectations separate dequeue results from the final size without changing any fact. Source example 1 also verifies both blocking events described in its explanation, while source example 2 permits exactly the scheduler-dependent multiset.

All eight ordinary fixtures are visible samples or trials. Exact boundaries cover capacity 1 and 30, producer and consumer thread counts 1 and 8, element 0 and 20, equal and greater enqueue counts, empty and nonempty final queues, and exactly 40 total method calls. Material semantics cover consumer-first empty blocking, full-queue producer blocking, capacity-one handoff, FIFO across interleaving, duplicate payloads, and concurrent producer ordering.

Protected, immutable native, and an independent condition-variable control passed all eight expected results. The same three implementations agreed on 120 seeded randomized balanced schedules: 59 began with a consumer, 61 with a producer, 42 included element 0, 49 included element 20, five used capacity 1, five used capacity 30, and six reached the randomized generator's maximum 39 calls. An unbounded control was rejected only after the semantic checkpoint detected its missing full-queue block.

`benchmark.json` remains absent, as required by the reviewed Original-18 route. The unchanged hidden complexity certificate contains no ordinary correctness inputs and validates bounded work, scheduler stress, semantic checking, and deadlock timeout evidence; real-test identifies `bounded_concurrency` rather than claiming a measured scaling verdict.
